title: USDA Lists Active New World Screwworm Case in Webb County
excerpt: The U.S. Department of Agriculture lists an active New World screwworm case in Webb County, involving livestock, after the Texas Animal Health Commission updated its infested zones to include Webb and Hidalgo counties, according to KGNS.
content:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture's online dashboard lists an active New World screwworm case in Webb County, according to KGNS.

The listing was posted Nov. 17, 2026, and involves livestock, the station reported. The Texas Animal Health Commission said it recently updated its infested zones after new cases in counties including Webb and Hidalgo.

Webb Watch previously reported confirmed screwworm cases in Starr and Zapata counties earlier this month. The Webb County listing puts the parasite's confirmed presence in Laredo's home county.

Pet and livestock owners should check animals daily for draining wounds, maggots or signs of discomfort, and call a veterinarian right away if they notice any of those signs, according to the report.

Update — November 20, 2026

The Webb County case is a calf in the northern part of the county, the Texas Animal Health Commission told KGNS on Nov. 19. The calf had a reported case in its navel, and samples submitted about 24 hours later confirmed screwworm, said Dr. Sandra Leyendecker, the commission’s Laredo region director. The U.S. Department of Agriculture listed the active livestock case on Nov. 17, and the commission’s interactive map shows the infested zone spreading across the Callaghan and Encinal areas. Webb County Judge Tano Tijerina said the county is monitoring the situation and urged the public to stay calm and follow state and federal guidance. Judge-elect Jerry Garza said he has begun discussions with local, state and federal partners about resources for ranchers and livestock producers. The commission issued new movement-restriction orders on Nov. 18 covering Dimmit, La Salle and Webb counties, and on Nov. 19 covering Medina and Uvalde counties. As of Nov. 19, the commission reported 81 confirmed premises across 27 Texas counties, according to its data tracked by The County Road.

Update — November 22, 2026

The Texas Animal Health Commission reported 90 confirmed screwworm premises across 29 Texas counties as of Nov. 22, up from 86 premises across 28 counties a day earlier, according to its data tracked by The County Road. The commission’s infested zone grew to 40 counties, adding Andrews, Martin and Midland counties in the Permian Basin. The commission issued four new executive director orders on Nov. 21, including a new order for Webb County and one covering Andrews, Martin and Midland counties. Animals in an infested zone may not move out of the zone without prior authorization from the commission. Nationally, the U.S. has recorded 149 screwworm cases since June, with 73 still active as of Nov. 19, according to Reuters.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 18, 2026. Nov. 20 update sources: KGNS, Nov. 19, 2026; Texas Animal Health Commission, Nov. 18–19, 2026; The County Road screwworm tracker, Nov. 19, 2026. Nov. 22 update sources: Texas Animal Health Commission, Nov. 21–22, 2026; The County Road screwworm tracker, Nov. 22, 2026; Reuters, Nov. 20, 2026.
